messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'heliotrope-prod' (tenant=heliotrope) reporting sustained GPU utilization >95% and request queueing. Pager sent to oncall-ml-sre.
oncall-ml-sre: I have the page, looking now. tagging infra and SRE.
maria-ops: seeing queue_length=320, p95 latency spiking to 6s for generation endpoints. GPU util 98% on node set gpua-*/pool-12.
alex-eng: logs show a sudden spike in bulk inference jobs from heliotrope starting ~00:18 UTC, many long-context runs (>=8k tokens). Possibly a training/validation loop accidentally hitting prod.
jordan-ml: confirmed — customer submitted large batch eval jobs via API key used for inference. We see repeated token_freeze patterns in the KV cache.
oncall-ml-sre: initial ask: do we want to auto-burst? policy says manual approval for enterprise bursts >2x baseline. We need a fast decision.
sam-csm: looping in Heliotrope CSM — reaching out now to confirm whether the batch job is intentional or accidental. If accidental they want it stopped. If intentional they'll accept brief degraded latency.
katy-security: heads-up: if we change routing or redirect, ensure audit log shows actions. Also check KMS usage stays normal.
oncall-ml-sre: mitigation options on table: 1) manual emergency burst (grant extra reserved GPUs to pool) 2) soft-throttle tenant (reduce concurrency/quota) 3) route tenant to a quantized/faster model fallback 4) evict low-priority jobs from pool. Need decision within 8 minutes to avoid widespread degradation.
alex-eng: technical note: fallback to gptj-quant reduces mean token time ~45% and frees KV memory. We can flip routing in ~30s. Command: ```rictl route set --tenant heliotrope --fallback-model gptj-quant --priority temporary```
maria-ops: eviction script ready: `scripts/drain_low_priority.sh pool-12 --tenant heliotrope --min-impact` — will drop queued non-interactive tasks.
oncall-ml-sre: Sam — any word from customer?
sam-csm: Heliotrope ops on the call, they say the batch was unintentional (CI job mis-targeted prod). They want it stopped and prefer not to burst. Requesting immediate throttle and assistance to scrub jobs.
jordan-ml: recommend: 1) enable tenant soft-throttle to 5 concurrent requests (from 50) 2) flip fallback to gptj-quant 3) run eviction script to clear queued bulk jobs.
oncall-ml-sre: doing throttle now: `rictl tenant set-quota heliotrope --concurrency 5 --reason "emergency throttle - suspected misdirected batch"`
oncall-ml-sre: applied fallback routing: `rictl route set --tenant heliotrope --fallback-model gptj-quant` — switching traffic now.
alex-eng: eviction running: `scripts/drain_low_priority.sh pool-12 --tenant heliotrope` — clearing ~260 queued tasks, should reduce queue in ~2m.
maria-ops: GPU util dropping to 68% after eviction and fallback, latency p95 down to 1.8s. Good initial signal.
sam-csm: Heliotrope confirmed they killed the CI job on their side. Appreciate the help. They asked for a short post-incident note and root cause once we stabilize.
katy-security: recorded actions in audit log and notified compliance channel. No anomalous KMS or creds usage.
jordan-ml: suggest we leave the fallback active for 1 hour and keep throttles for 30 minutes, then gradually restore. Also propose follow-up: create a tenant-level guardrail to block bulk evals on prod keys by default.
oncall-ml-sre: agreed. I'll keep monitoring for 45 minutes. Creating incident ticket now and assigning postmortem to eng/infra + CSM + security.
incident-bot: Incident channel created: #incident-6881234567-heliotrope-gpu-surge. Pager cleared. :white_check_mark:
maria-ops: note for postmortem: timeline, commands run, metrics (gpu_util, queue_length, p95), customer confirmation, and proposed tenant guardrail.
alex-eng: small follow-up — one node shows elevated memory fragmentation, will schedule a maintenance reboot during off-peak. Not impacting current traffic.
oncall-ml-sre: closing live page. If any regressions ping me. Great cross-team response — nice work. :clap:
sam-csm: Heliotrope appreciates the quick mitigation. They requested a follow-up call later today to review guardrails and possible dedicated burst policy adjustments.
incident-bot: Monitoring for 60m; will auto-close channel if no regressions.
